**Review Result**

Quality score: **6/10**. The code is readable, compact, and has a useful test suite: `61 passed`. I would not approve it as-is because the ingest/update logic can corrupt accounting data when dumps arrive out of order or contain corrected resource fields.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **120 lines**. Most of that is fixing lifecycle freshness logic, timestamp normalization, validation, DB indexing, CLI report DB handling, and adding regression tests.

**Findings**

- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70): High: Same-rank records are blindly updated, so an older RUNNING or terminal snapshot can overwrite newer `elapsed_sec`, `end`, and `exit_code`.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74): High: The “unchanged” check ignores `user`, `partition`, `alloc_cpus`, `gpus`, and `exit_code`, so corrected accounting fields with the same state/end/elapsed are silently discarded.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:31): High: Unknown states default to terminal rank, so active Slurm states not listed here can block later legitimate transitions.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152): Medium: Required fields like `User`, `Partition`, and `ExitCode` are not validated for blank values before insertion/reporting.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:176): Medium: Header/data parsing only strips `\n`, so CRLF input can reject an otherwise valid header or retain `\r` in `ExitCode`.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118): Medium: Offset-aware timestamps are accepted and stored as mixed ISO strings, while report filtering uses lexicographic SQLite comparisons.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:65): Medium: Time filters and `MAX(COALESCE(...))` depend on string ordering, which is fragile unless timestamps are normalized to one timezone/format.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13): Medium: The schema has no indexes for reference-time, state, user, or partition report paths, so reports become full-table scans as history grows.
- [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121): Medium: Report commands call `db.connect`, which creates a new empty DB for a typo or missing path instead of surfacing an operator error.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13): Low: No schema versioning or migrations are present, so future schema changes will be brittle once users have local DBs.
- [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:13): Low: Development tooling is minimal; there is no configured formatter, linter, type checker, or coverage target.
- [tests/test_ingest.py](/work/tests/test_ingest.py:56): Low: Tests cover rank downgrade prevention but miss same-rank stale snapshots and corrected resource-field regressions.

issues.description: Same-rank records are blindly updated, allowing older RUNNING or terminal snapshots to overwrite newer accounting data.
The unchanged check ignores user, partition, alloc_cpus, gpus, and exit_code, so corrected accounting fields can be silently discarded.
Unknown states default to terminal rank, which can block valid transitions from unlisted active Slurm states.
Required fields such as User, Partition, and ExitCode are accepted when blank.
CRLF input is not stripped correctly, causing valid headers to be rejected or carriage returns to leak into field values.
Offset-aware timestamps are accepted without normalization, creating mixed timestamp formats in storage.
Report filtering and newest-time selection rely on lexicographic string ordering for timestamps.
The jobs table has no indexes for report filters or grouping paths, so reports will full-scan growing history.
Report commands create an empty database for a missing or mistyped path instead of failing clearly.
The schema has no versioning or migration mechanism for future DB changes.
Development tooling only installs pytest, with no formatter, linter, type checker, or coverage configuration.
Ingest tests miss same-rank stale snapshot and corrected accounting-field regression cases.
